headline: Light rain today and through Sunday, then a wetter, windier pattern starting next week.
summary: A high-pressure ridge, a dome of sinking, drier air, is moving inland and ending the cool, foggy stretch. A weather system sitting offshore will keep light rain going through Sunday, with light snow in the mountains and little at the passes. Morning fog could freeze in the valleys, and highs will reach the 40s to near 50. Next week turns wetter and windier as a deeper low forms offshore, bringing repeated rounds of rain, mountain snow, gusty winds, and a growing threat of coastal flooding. Forecasters are fairly confident about the weekend but less sure of the timing and strength of next week's systems.
changes: Rain now starts this afternoon rather than tonight, and the later forecast describes a modest chance of storm-force gusts next week. The earlier discussion's possible Skokomish River flooding did not come up in the later one.
